chapter: Sherwood, big bands and sound concept
title: Leonard Feather's Down Beat Blindfold Test and the Sherwood record
summary: Feather played the Sherwood overdub record, not knowing Rudy made it; Don finds the 1954 listing 'One Man Band'.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: And they did a…you did a Downbeat blindfold test.
Oh yeah, I know what you’re talking about. Leonard Feather, he had a column in Downbeat called “Blindfold Test” and I did it once. What was the record though?
He played the Bobby Sherwood one.

Oh yeah. He knew it was an overdub, Leonard Feather knew it, but he didn’t know I did it. So he’s sitting there trying to catch me with the blindfold test (Laughs). And it was the last one of the tests. So he says, “Listen to this Rudy, tell me what you think it is.” So he puts this record on and I laughed. I said, “I made that,” and he didn’t know that. Somewhere here there is a copy of that, not the record, the issue. I’m sure its in the Downbeat files. You made reference to that.
I’m looking for it. Here it is.
1954 Bobby Sherwood, “One Man Bad.” Bobby Sherwood: four trumpet parts, mellophone, trombone, vibes, piano, guitar, bass, drums, and four vocal parts.
Right, I forgot the vocals! (Laughs) So we did that, and Leonard Feather played that back to me, expecting I don’t know what. I started laughing. I’m glad you remembered that, I would have forgot.
So Bobby Sherwood was the one who brought Bobby Sherwood to you?
Bob Theil, musically, he was like the A&R man.
So did he do the session, or was it just you and Bobby?
Just Bobby Sherwood came out. I’d love to have a copy of that. That’s a wonderful book you have there.
Yeah, well of course the subject of that is Rudy Van Gelder
You put that together, I’ll bet.
